title: Highest temperature in NYC on September 5?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and private model runs converge on a high temperature near 80°F for New York City on September 5, driven by northerly flow behind a departing front that advects cooler, drier air while skies remain mostly sunny. This places the outcome squarely in the 80-81°F bin favored by traders at 55.5% implied probability, consistent with the long-term Central Park average of 79.8°F and the absence of strong warm-air advection or subsidence that would push readings higher. Light northerly winds of 5–10 mph will limit mixing and keep the urban heat island effect modest, while any increase in afternoon cloud cover could trim the peak by a degree or two. Updated model guidance and morning observations on the 5th remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift the tight 78–83°F cluster of probabilities.
